name: St. Paul's parish school, Clinton Street

function.note: St. Paul's Catholic School (Sisters of Loretto), Clinton Street corner Mather, 1868-1871 (Andreas vol. 2; Edwards 1871 lists St. Paul's school at Clinton corner Mather).

research_note: ST. PAUL'S PARISH SCHOOL, built by T-3831 for the 1871 scene: 'the parish school $5,000' (Andreas vol. 2, p. 406), 'St. Paul's Parish School, $5,000' among the fire's Catholic losses (Sheahan and Upton), kept by the Sisters of Loretto at Clinton Street corner Mather from 1868 to 1871. Where it stood on the parish's ground and how it looked are not recorded: it is set on Clinton Street north of the priest's house and drawn as a two-storey frame school.

documented_range.note: Standing on the night of the fire, which destroyed it (Andreas vol. 2, pp. 406, 712-718).

position.symbolic_location: Clinton Street north of St. Paul's Church.
position.note: On the parish's ground at Clinton and Mather (Andreas vol. 2; Edwards 1871); its place on Clinton Street north of the priest's house is reconstructed. The footprint's origin is local E -246.2 N -1503.0.

derivation.reason: Laid out from the accounts' description of the block against the 1871 plan's streets; no traced frontage for the 1871 city is in data/traces/street_control.json to recompute it from.

footprint.note: Reconstructed: a frame school of the size its $5,000 cost bought.

fire.note: 'St. Paul's Parish School, $5,000', among the Catholic losses (Sheahan and Upton 1871); destroyed with the church (Andreas vol. 2, p. 406).

blocks.name: the school
blocks.note: A two-storey frame schoolhouse with its gable to Clinton Street, the size a $5,000 school of 1868 bought (Andreas vol. 2, p. 406; Sheahan and Upton). No picture or plan is known; its form is reconstructed.

towers.name: the bell-cote
towers.note: A small bell-cote on the school's front gable, reconstructed.

value.note: ST. PAUL'S PARISH SCHOOL, built by T-3831: the Sisters of Loretto's school at Clinton and Mather, 1868-1871 (Andreas vol. 2, p. 406 and the list of schools), reconstructed.

composition.note: ST. PAUL'S PARISH SCHOOL, built by T-3831: the Sisters of Loretto's school at Clinton and Mather, 1868-1871 (Andreas vol. 2, p. 406 and the list of schools), reconstructed.

wall_material.value: Painted clapboard on a frame, a shingle roof
wall_material.note: Reconstructed as the West Side's frame buildings.

phases.change_note: Built T-3831 (2026-11-28): drawn in the 1871 scene on the landmark_1871 archetype, in place of the generic context fill that stood on its lot.
